question: Road transport is a driving force of the European economy, with trucks handling 75 % of the total volume of road freight and almost 90 % of the value of all freight Europe-wide.

Despite the EU’s efforts to develop safe and secure truck parking areas (SSTPAs)1, there is still a significant shortage of such infrastructure across the European road network and the few facilities that do exist offer very substandard services.

Not only does this lack of infrastructure worsen the working conditions of professional drivers who are deprived of safe rest areas, it also undermines road safety2as most accidents are caused by the human factor3, including fatigue resulting from bad working conditions. What is more, the lack of SSTPAs puts workers at risk of potential physical assault and increases the risk of cargo theft. In view of the above: 1.

Does it intend to boost European funding further to ramp up the construction of SSTPAs so as to improve the working conditions of drivers and make the profession more attractive to potential young drivers?

Does it plan to put together a European strategy or a targeted plan for the creation of an extensive connected network of parking areas that will cover the entire EU road network and will speed up the achievement of the set target of one SSTPA every 150 km?

Article 31(4) of the new TEN-T Regulation states that by 2040 Member States must ensure the development of SSTPAs along the roads of the core network and extended core network, or within 3 km driving distance from the nearest exit of the road of the trans-European network, with an average maximum distance of 150 km between two such areas (https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/PE-56-2024-REV-1/En/pdf).

Among other things, these areas make it possible to install modern infrastructure such as electric charging stations and alternative fuel facilities, necessary for the decarbonisation of the sector. In a survey carried out by the ETFA, 60 % of the professional drivers questioned said they regularly felt tired when driving due to a shortage of secure parking areas, among other things. See https://www.etfeurope.
org/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/Fatigue_SUMMARY_EN_.pdf. See https://www.iru.org/what-we-do/being-trusted-voice-mobility-and-logistics/people/road-safety
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (23.1.2025) 1. The Commission has been supporting, through the Connecting Europe Facility (CEF), the development of new and the upgrade of existing parking areas to meet these standards. In total, CEF has so far co-funded 138 parking areas and around 16,113 parking spots with EUR 231,5 million.

Further opportunities can be explored under the CEF 2024 call closing on 21 January 2025. Support for safe and secure parking areas (SSPAs) for heavy duty vehicles is also envisaged under the Member States Cohesion Policy Programmes 2021-27. 2.

In order to guarantee access to adequate resting facilities for professional drivers, the revised trans-European transport network (TEN-T) Regulation1 sets out a new requirement obliging Member States to deploy safe and secure parking areas on the core and extended network every 150 km on average by 2040.

The Commission is currently carrying-out a study in order to better understand the current demand and supply of SSPAs and forecast future needs. These findings will be key to guide future private and public investment.

Based on this study, the Commission will present in the first half of 2025 a report to the European Parliament and the Council on the availability of SSPAs and suitable rest facilities for drivers together with suggestions on how to reinforce and best support the development of SSPAs in the future.
1 Regulation (EU) 2024/1679 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 June 2024 on Union
guidelines for the development of the trans-European transport network, amending Regulations (EU) 2021/1153 and (EU) No 913/2010 and repealing Regulation (EU) No 1315/2013.
